text:
mina: hey everyone, first week question // pair-programming with a contractor and hit 429s. We were sharing one hosted key via a local proxy to avoid rotating for the contractor. Bad idea?

ton y: yeah that's tough. Sharing a hosted key is risky and will chew through quota quickly. For short pairing sessions use a sandbox key or request a temporary CI/staging key scoped to the contractor.

mina: how do sandbox quotas work vs hosted? I thought sandbox was unlimited for experiments.

de von: sandbox has lower per-key rate limits and is intended for dev/experiments. Hosted keys have higher quotas but are production and billed. Quotas are applied per-key and sometimes per-org depending on the plan. If you proxy multiple devs through one hosted key you'll incur combined rate usage and likely hit token/burst limits.

mina: is there a fast path to get a temp higher quota for pair-programming?

leah: yes - post in #devex with: repo, purpose (pairing/contractor), duration, and expected RPS. We can issue a short-lived sandbox CI key or a scoped hosted staging key for up to 48-72h. Use the template: "Temp key request - repo: X, purpose: pairing, duration: 24h, expected RPS: 5".

mina: curious about practical mitigation while waiting: any local patterns to reduce 429s?

ton y: a few things we do: 1) add client-side token bucket limiter (leaky bucket) to keep steady QPS, 2) add jittered exponential backoff honoring Retry-After header, 3) for streaming responses batch smaller or use shorter max_tokens during testing, 4) swap heavy loops for mocked responses in unit tests.

mina: streaming note: we were seeing partial streams then 429 mid-stream. Is that expected?

de von: yes, streaming still consumes tokens; if the request crosses the quota threshold mid-request you can get a 429 while receiving tokens. For long streams reduce stream chunk size or move to a staging key during heavy experiments.

infra-bot: :warning: Security policy reminder: hosted API keys must not be shared outside approved secrets stores. If a hosted key is leaked or pushed, rotate immediately and notify security@redwood.ai. Automated repo scans will flag exposures.

mina: what about contractors—can they get sandbox keys or do they need a different flow?

leah: contractors can get sandbox keys tied to a short-lived ticket. For longer engagements we provision scoped staging keys and require an NDA + access review. Open a #devex ticket stating contractor name, org, repo, duration.

mina: quick checklist for others who hit this: 1) avoid proxying multiple devs through one hosted key, 2) use sandbox for local dev/pairing, 3) request temp CI/staging key via #devex with template, 4) implement client-side rate limits and backoff, 5) mock heavy tests.

ton y: also watch headers: X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, and Retry-After if present. Logging those helps debug who exhausted quota.

mina: thanks all, I'll open a devex ticket for a 24h sandbox key for the contractor and switch our proxy to use it during pairing. saved the checklist! :thumbsup:
